test_title: PYST 65: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held  On 29 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the phrase/idiom that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

When our principal said she was leaving the company, I __played out the opportunity__ to fill the job.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"jumped at the opportunity"** is an idiomatic expression meaning to** eagerly seize a chance.**
 
• It correctly conveys the intended meaning of taking advantage quickly and enthusiastically.
 
• The other options **(glided, started, ran) **are not commonly used in this context and do not fit the idiomatic usage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When our principal said she was leaving the company, I **jumped at the opportunity** to fill the job."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glided at the opportunity:** "Glided" implies a smooth movement and does not convey eagerness or seizing a chance.
 
• **Started at the opportunity:** "Started" can imply beginning something but does not fit idiomatically to mean eagerly taking a chance.
 
• **Ran to the opportunity:** "Ran" suggests physical movement towards something but is not idiomatic for seizing an opportunity.
